notes: The shared WebSearch budget ran out after the first article, so this article could not be freshly researched. Every fact comes from the writer-kit known-good table or the repo fact-check notes (PART 3), which were themselves built from search-index summaries. Please re-verify before publishing: (1) The ovality formula (Dmax - Dmin)/Dnominal x 100, sourced in the notes to The Fabricator and the IMEKO TC14 2007 paper. (2) Engineers Edge's alternative formula dividing by (Dmax + Dmin): the notes give the URL 'as surfaced in search results' (ns1.engineersedge.com host); confirm the exact formula on the live page. (3) 'The Fabricator has cited ovality tolerances from roughly 1.5% to 8% depending on end use': the notes do not record the exact article URL, so it is attributed in the text but not linked; please find and link it, or cut the sentence. (4) Rogue Fab thin-wall roller: 'deformation about 5-7% vs about 10% without' (capacity chart, via notes). (5) The Fabricator mandrel example (2 x .065 on 4 in CLR: WF 30.8, D 2.0, two-ball mandrel with wiper). (6) SCCA Time Trials 3x tube diameter bend radius (kit says re-verify wording). The worked-example readings (1.790 / 1.700 on 1.750 nominal) and the 1.5/3/5/8% rows of the limit table are labelled in the text as made-up numbers to show the arithmetic, not typical results or recommended limits. Left out as unverifiable: forum pressure-based limits (8% below / 5% above 600 psi), any code clause numbers (e.g. pressure-piping flattening limits), Rogue Fab's '0.9% deformation' 1D exhaust bend (image alt text only), and any rulebook ovality limit. A calipers product box would suit this article, but no calipers ASIN could be verified once the search budget was exhausted; the WFB2 box (kit-verified ASINs) is used instead. Editor may add a verified calipers box.
